newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura head intends to resign after probe - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Nomura head intends to resign after probe - Jiji.

text.p: The president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Hideo Sakamaki, intends to resign after Japan's securities watchdog completes an investigation into irregular deals at the firm, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
Jiji said Sakamaki told the news agency that he intended to resign to take management responsibility for an incident announced by the company on Thursday.
But a Nomura spokeman said the brokerage's public relations office knew nothing about Sakamaki's intentions, and could not comment further.
On Thursday, Nomura publicly admitted that it was highly likely that two of its directors had been involved in illegal deals.

Nomura vice president Atsushi Saito told reporters Nomura had found out that the directors made deals regarded as discretionary transactions with a corporate client, and they also transferred profits from Nomura's own account to the client's account.
He said that both of the actions are illegal, and that the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) was investigating.

Saito said he could not at the moment confirm media reports that the corporate client was run by a relative of a "sokaiya" racketeer, but he added that the client had a longstanding relationship with the two directors and family ties to a Nomura shareholder.
Sokaiya, often linked to Japan's "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices.
